title: Training on GPU | CatBoost
why_relevant: Confirms how to enable GPU training and select devices, needed to keep local_gpu and kaggle_gpu on the same CatBoost pipeline.
extracted_technique: Use task_type='GPU' and devices='0' (or range) for CatBoost training; keep other params consistent across environments.
query: catboost.ai documentation GPU training task_type devices
takeaway: CatBoost supports GPU training via task_type='GPU' and a devices parameter. This enables longer schedules while keeping the algorithm identical between local and Kaggle execution.

title: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features (NeurIPS 2018)
why_relevant: Primary source for CatBoost’s ordered boosting and categorical handling, directly relevant to high-cardinality categorical regression and leakage-avoidance in CV.
extracted_technique: Ordered boosting / ordered target statistics to reduce prediction shift from target leakage in boosting with categorical features.
query: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features NeurIPS 2018 pdf
takeaway: CatBoost introduces ordered boosting and a categorical processing scheme designed to reduce a kind of leakage-induced prediction shift. It is a strong default for tabular problems dominated by high-cardinality categorical variables.

title: HashingVectorizer — scikit-learn documentation
why_relevant: Supports a practical, leak-resistant sparse text/ID feature pipeline for pay-item descriptions/IDs without storing a vocabulary, suitable for large raw tables.
extracted_technique: Hashing trick for stateless sparse token features; choose large n_features to reduce collisions; combine with linear regression on log1p target.
takeaway: HashingVectorizer is fast, memory-efficient, and stateless, making it well-suited for large token spaces like pay_item_id and pay_item_description. It reduces leakage risk versus fitting a vocabulary on combined train+test.

title: mean_squared_log_error — scikit-learn documentation
why_relevant: Defines MSLE/RMSLE computation and provides a reliable reference implementation detail for offline CV scoring in log space.
extracted_technique: Compute RMSLE via mean_squared_log_error(..., squared=False) on non-negative predictions; train on log1p(total_bid) and clip expm1 outputs at 0.
query: sklearn.metrics.mean_squared_log_error documentation squared False root mean squared logarithmic error
takeaway: RMSLE is the square root of MSLE over log1p values, so training on log1p targets is natural. Predictions must be non-negative before applying log-based scoring, motivating clipping at 0.
